uncertain.note: page quality: the leaf is clean, sharply printed and evenly inked; every line is legible at native resolution. A pale brown damp-stain runs across the upper outer corner, crossing the head margin and touching the folio '62' and the first two body lines without obscuring any letter. Show-through of the recto is visible over the whole text area as a faint grey ghost, never confusable with type. Nothing is lost to damage or to the crop; the strip of the facing page along the right (gutter) edge has been ignored throughout.

counts for the reconciler: 30 printed lines in the body column = 28 text lines in 4 paragraph blocks (2 + 4 + 20 + 2) plus 2 display lines ('TEXTE.', 'ANNOTAT. XLI.'). No markers, no margin notes, no foot citations, no signature, no catchword, no ornament and no decorated initial. The page has three type sizes: the small annotation fount (blocks[0], blocks[5]), the italic verse fount (blocks[1]) and the large TEXTE fount (blocks[3]).

the outer (left) margin is completely blank on this page: all four margin strips show bare paper, and there is no marker letter anywhere in the body. margin_notes and foot_notes are therefore empty by observation, not by omission.

continues_prev: the page opens mid-sentence with 'c'eſt à dire raboteux' — the tail of a gloss begun on p061, which is not yet transcribed, so the judgement rests on the sense alone. continues_next is set true because the block's last line ends 'quand il dit,' and runs straight into the Latin distich that follows; the reconciler may prefer false on the ground that the paragraph block itself ends there.

the four italic Latin lines (Q. Serenus Sammonicus, Liber medicinalis) are set apart and indented but are quoted verse, so they are recorded as one paragraph block with one string per printed line, per §6, not as headings. Line 2 overruns and its turn-over 'hæſit,' is indented further; it is kept as its own line and not joined to the line above.

sic, wrong sort: the print reads 'teſmoius' for 'teſmoins'. Checked at 8x — after the dotted i the sort is an unmistakable u (bowl joined at the baseline, two full stems with foot serifs), not an n (which in this fount has a shoulder springing from the top of the left stem; compare 'ont' and 'nepueu' below). Transcribed as printed per §7.

uncertain.text: rir le priſonnier. ce que ledit Loze reffu-
uncertain.note: 'reffu-' is a genuine double f, not an ſſ misread: at 16x both tall sorts carry a full crossbar projecting on BOTH sides of the stem and a foot serif on the baseline, where the long s of this fount (e.g. 'aſſeuré' two lines below) has only a left-hand nub and no foot serif. 'reffuſa' is a normal period spelling of refusa; not emended. Flagged because reader B is likely to write 'reſſu-'.

uncertain.text: pourſuite contre la volonté de ladit. de
uncertain.note: a small, very lightly inked point stands on the baseline after 'ladit' (abbreviating 'ladite'), clearly separated from the following 'de'. At 16x it is a round baseline dot, much fainter than the points in 'aud.' and 'priſonnier.' but larger and darker than the paper specks around it. Read as an abbreviation point; reader B may take it for a speck and write 'ladit de'.

uncertain.text: ne doit pas eſtre de petite vertu: car nous ſommes en
uncertain.note: ESCALATE. The first sort of 'eſtre' carries a distinct hook descending below the baseline from the bottom of the bowl, exactly where a cedilla sits, so the print may read 'çſtre' (a wrong sort) rather than 'eſtre'. At 20x the bowl does appear to carry the mid-bar of an e (compare the unambiguous e of 'de' immediately following, and the bar-less c of 'car' on the same line), which is why 'eſtre' is given as the reading; but the descender is solid black, the same weight as the type, and is not matched anywhere else on the page. Nothing prints below this line (it is the last line of the page), so it cannot be an ascender from a line beneath. Needs a third eye.

punctuation checked by shape, not by sense: after 'mourir' there are two marks, a dot at x-height above a comma with a tail below the baseline — a semicolon, not a comma. After 'priſonnier' there is a single round dot on the baseline — a period — although the next word 'iuſqu'à' begins with a lower-case i. Same pattern on lines[8] ('priſonnier. ce que'). Transcribed as printed.

uncertain.note: 'ſes femme & beaux fils' is what is printed (ſ-e-s at 10x, a plural article governing both nouns); not emended to 'ſa femme'. The comma after 'Guerre' has a clear tail below the baseline.

uncertain.note: the line ends 'mou' with no word-break hyphen and runs on to 'rir' on the next line. Normal for this print (§1); recorded only so the reconciler does not read it as an omission.
